programs.name: hazards
programs.title: Hazards, one at a time
programs.watch: Step from reset. Cycle 4: add t2,t0,t1 takes t0 from MEM/WB and t1 from EX/MEM. Cycle 9: addi t6,t5,1 waits in ID for one cycle while lw t5 is in EX (load-use stall). Cycle 16: bne is taken and the two instructions fetched after it are flushed.
programs.source:
# Forwarding and stalls, instruction by instruction.
# Step through this one: every dependent pair is deliberate.
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    li   t0, 40            # t0 = 40
    li   t1, 2             # t1 = 2
    add  t2, t0, t1        # 42   t0 from MEM/WB, t1 from EX/MEM  -> two forwards
    sub  t3, t2, t1        # 40   t2 from EX/MEM (just computed)
    xor  t4, t3, t2        # 2    t3 from EX/MEM, t2 from MEM/WB
    la   a1, buf
    sw   t4, 0(a1)         # store the forwarded value
    lw   t5, 0(a1)         # load it back
    addi t6, t5, 1         # 3    load-use: the pipeline must stall one cycle
    lw   a2, 4(a1)         # a2 = 100 (from .data)
    nop                    # one independent instruction after the load...
    add  a3, a2, t6        # 103  ...so this needs no stall (MEM/WB forward)
    beq  a3, t6, wrong     # not taken: fall through
    bne  a3, t6, done      # taken: two younger instructions are flushed
    li   a0, 0
    li   a0, 0
wrong:
    li   a0, 0xbad
    ebreak
done:
    mv   a0, a3            # a0 = 103
    ebreak
    .data
buf: .word 0
    .word 100

programs.name: branches
programs.title: Counting loop
programs.watch: Nine taken branches, each flushing two wrongly fetched instructions (the core predicts not-taken); the last blt falls through.
programs.source:
# A counting loop: one taken branch per iteration, flushed fetches each time.
# Sums 1..10 into a0 (55); a1 counts iterations.
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    li   a0, 0
    li   a1, 0
    li   a2, 10
loop:
    addi a1, a1, 1
    add  a0, a0, a1
    blt  a1, a2, loop      # taken 9 times, not taken once
    ebreak

programs.name: sum
programs.title: Load-use: naive vs scheduled
programs.watch: The first loop stalls one cycle per element (lw immediately followed by add). The second loop does the same work with the pointer and counter updates moved between them: no stalls.
programs.source:
# Sum an array two ways. The naive loop puts the load right before its use
# (one stall per element); the scheduled loop reorders so the pointer and
# counter updates fill the slot. Both sums land in a0 and a1 (both 1240).
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    la   t0, data
    li   t1, 8
    li   a0, 0
naive:
    lw   t2, 0(t0)
    add  a0, a0, t2        # load-use stall here, every iteration
    addi t0, t0, 4
    addi t1, t1, -1
    bnez t1, naive

    la   t0, data
    li   t1, 8
    li   a1, 0
scheduled:
    lw   t2, 0(t0)
    addi t0, t0, 4         # independent work covers the load latency
    addi t1, t1, -1
    add  a1, a1, t2        # value arrives from MEM/WB, no stall
    bnez t1, scheduled
    ebreak
    .data
data: .word 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 960

programs.name: multiply
programs.title: Shift-and-add multiply
programs.watch: andi t0 -> beqz t0 is a forwarded compare; the loop runs 9 times for a 9-bit multiplier.
programs.source:
# Shift-and-add multiplication, the way libgcc does it for RV32I.
# a0 = 123 * 456 = 56088 (0xDB18)
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    li   a1, 123           # multiplicand
    li   a2, 456           # multiplier
    li   a0, 0
mul_loop:
    andi t0, a2, 1
    beqz t0, skip
    add  a0, a0, a1
skip:
    slli a1, a1, 1
    srli a2, a2, 1
    bnez a2, mul_loop
    ebreak

programs.name: memcopy
programs.title: Byte copy and word copy
programs.watch: lbu/sb pairs then lw/sw pairs; the store data is forwarded from the load result in WB. Both destination buffers fill in the memory view.
programs.result: a0 = 32; dst_bytes and dst_words equal src.
programs.source:
# Copy 16 bytes from src to dst, first byte by byte, then word by word
# into a second buffer. Watch both destinations fill in the memory view.
# a0 = number of bytes copied (32).
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    la   t0, src
    la   t1, dst_bytes
    li   t2, 16
bytes:
    lbu  t3, 0(t0)
    sb   t3, 0(t1)
    addi t0, t0, 1
    addi t1, t1, 1
    addi t2, t2, -1
    bnez t2, bytes

    la   t0, src
    la   t1, dst_words
    li   t2, 4
words:
    lw   t3, 0(t0)
    sw   t3, 0(t1)
    addi t0, t0, 4
    addi t1, t1, 4
    addi t2, t2, -1
    bnez t2, words
    li   a0, 32
    ebreak
    .data
src:       .ascii "silicon gates ok"
    .align 2
dst_bytes: .space 16
dst_words: .space 16

programs.name: calls
programs.title: Calls and a stack frame
programs.watch: jal writes ra from PC+4 in WB; ret is a jalr whose target comes from a forwarded ra. sp moves down and back up in the register file.
programs.source:
# Function calls with jal/jalr and a stack frame: square(7) + square(5) = 74.
# ra and sp move; every call and return redirects the front end.
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    la   sp, stack_top
    li   a0, 7
    call square            # jal ra, square
    mv   s0, a0
    li   a0, 5
    call square
    add  a0, a0, s0        # 74
    ebreak

square:                    # a0 = a0 * a0 by repeated addition
    addi sp, sp, -8
    sw   ra, 4(sp)
    sw   s1, 0(sp)
    mv   s1, a0
    li   t0, 0
    mv   t1, a0
1:  add  t0, t0, s1
    addi t1, t1, -1
    bnez t1, 1b
    mv   a0, t0
    lw   s1, 0(sp)
    lw   ra, 4(sp)
    addi sp, sp, 8
    ret                    # jalr x0, 0(ra)
    .data
    .space 64
stack_top:

crt0:
# Silicon C runtime: stack at top of RAM, zeroed .bss, call main, halt with
# main's return value left in a0.
    .section .text.start
    .globl _start
_start:
    la   sp, __stack_top
    la   t0, __bss_start
    la   t1, __bss_end
1:  bgeu t0, t1, 2f
    sw   zero, 0(t0)
    addi t0, t0, 4
    j    1b
2:  call main
    ebreak
